about.title: Pismo Beach Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Pismo Beach residents and visitors who need medical care often end up treated at clinics and hospitals serving San Luis Obispo County, and most of the time that care goes fine. But when a provider misses a diagnosis, makes a surgical mistake, or mismanages medication, the harm can follow a patient long after they leave the exam room. Medical malpractice cases are different from a typical injury claim — California requires a qualified medical expert to review the care and confirm it fell below the accepted standard, and there are strict notice and filing deadlines under MICRA. LawProactive doesn't practice law or evaluate your medical records ourselves. We simply listen to what happened, then connect you with an independent California attorney who focuses on these cases and can tell you, plainly, whether your situation looks like malpractice or simply a difficult medical outcome. There's no cost to start that conversation.

whyChoose.title: What to Know Before You Move Forward

items.title: MICRA's Clock Moves Fast
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from when you discovered the harm, and never more than three years from the injury itself, to bring a malpractice claim. A 90-day pre-suit notice to the provider is also required, so waiting to ask questions can quietly cost you options.

items.title: An Expert Has to Back the Claim
items.desc: Under California law, a qualified medical expert almost always has to review the case and confirm the care fell below the accepted standard. A poor outcome by itself isn't enough — the attorney you're connected with can help sort out whether the facts actually support a claim.

items.title: Non-Economic Damages Are Capped, But the Cap Rises
items.desc: California law places a statutory limit on non-economic damages in malpractice cases, and that cap increases each year by law. An independent attorney can explain how that cap and other rules could apply to your specific situation.

items.question: How long do I have to file a medical malpractice claim after treatment in Pismo Beach?
items.answer: Under MICRA, it's generally one year from when you discovered or reasonably should have discovered the injury, and no more than three years from the date of the injury itself. There's also a required 90-day notice to the healthcare provider before a lawsuit can be filed. Because these deadlines can be easy to miss, it helps to ask an attorney early rather than waiting.

items.question: I had a bad outcome after surgery — does that automatically mean malpractice?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California law requires showing the provider's care fell below the accepted medical standard, and that usually takes a qualified medical expert's review. A difficult or unexpected outcome, even a serious one, isn't the same thing as malpractice on its own.

items.question: Does LawProactive handle malpractice claims for Pismo Beach patients directly?
items.answer: No — LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm, and we don't represent clients or give legal advice. We simply listen to what happened at your appointment or hospital stay and connect you with an independent California attorney who takes malpractice cases on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless they recover money for you.
